- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast gently, especially near lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 30d mean), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10–15% above peak or adjust downward after 2–3 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, not just price history.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 30d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 (neutral) followed by 1.00 (positive), model often fails to capture the positive momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% on next day if sentiment turns positive.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust future forecast downward by 0.5–1% per day to reflect mean reversion or sentiment decay.
